A baker sells the best bread in town for
one copper coin. And so he's working 18 hours a day, but he's barely surviving.
One day, an old merchant sees him turn away customers halfway through the day
when he runs out of bread. He says, "Just double your prices." And of
course, the baker is like, "That's impossible. Lose all my customers." But
eventually, he's like, "Fine, I'll double my prices." And when he does, he
loses half his customers. But he makes the same money working half the time.
And with his free hours, he then experiments with new recipes, and his
bread gets even better, and he sells even more. And over time he keeps
selling more until eventually he doubles his prices again. And so a year later he
sold the same number of lows he used to but at four times the price to his
favorite customers because they valued the quality over the price. And so the
merchant then said to him, "The price you charge is how valuable you tell the
